label: <DEL> step of long sequences starting with 0 (about to output 0)
explanation: Very sparse feature (73 activations in 1M sequences, one per sequence). Fires only at the delimiter step (100% of mass), only for L = 8 or 9 (84% of mass at L = 9), and almost always when the first original token, i.e. the token being output at <DEL>, is the digit 0 (97% of mass; the rest are first_tok c). The predicate (<DEL>, first_tok 0, L >= 8) covers 95% of activations and 97% of mass, but only ~0.7% of matching steps fire, so precision is very poor; restricting to L == 9 or to specific second tokens (c, w) raises precision only to ~7% at a large recall cost. Strongest activations tend to have second token c or w (0 c ..., 0 w ...), but there is no clean rule. Never fires in the original or copy phases, on short sequences, or when the output token is not 0/c.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 18 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=0 (+4.60), orig2=u (+1.91), next_out=c (+1.56), orig3=u (+1.42), prev_tok=z (+1.22), orig1=c (+1.12). Lower it: in_count=1 (-2.27), in_first=0 (-1.83), orig8=- (-1.79), orig7=- (-1.66).
